subject: Tech Accelerator - Check-in & Cyber Valley Webinar Monday
text:
OFFICIAL

Good morning all,

Thank you to everyone who joined Tuesday’s online session with ZF and e-mobil BW. We hope the discussion with Sebastian was valuable and that he becomes a useful contact for you moving forward.

While turnout from other ZF colleagues and externals was lower than expected – a common challenge with doing these formats online – Sebastian is very committed to supporting the cohort, and we’ve agreed to follow up with
 everyone who initially signed up. Please keep us updated on any 1:1s you arrange with ZF colleagues.

We won’t be sending out a formal feedback survey on this session, but if you have any comments or suggestions, please reach out to us.

Cyber Valley x ARENA2036 Webinar – Monday 24 November

• 
Agenda: Final version attached.

• 
Format:

• 
The session will focus on a Q&A with Alexander Rudolf (Alex) Diehl, Cyber Valley’s senior advisor. Alex is highly connected (including within the German Bundestag),
 involved in Gigafactory Europe, and an active angel investor. He has reviewed your company profiles and is briefed on the Accelerator.

• 
We’ve drafted a few starter questions, but this is your opportunity to seek advice. If possible, please send us some questions in advance, so we can share these
 with Alex.

• 
Instead of full pitches, we suggest a short overview of your company plus any pain points, ICP, or specific questions you’d like to raise.

• 
The hosts will also have the opportunity to ask you questions.

• 
Timing: We may finish earlier but have scheduled two hours for flexibility.

•

subject: Re: Encord/Tau Robotics - Services for G1_Mobile Project
text:
Hi Alyssa,

sure, let's do it by email if you prefer that. Here is my feedback:
I think there was a fundamental misunderstanding of my reviews. For
example, there is no rule to "to give a score of 1 if the item is dropped
before the instruction ends".

The score should be labelled like this:
Pretend that you are giving these instructions to the robot to accomplish
some goal. The score is simply how much you like the behavior of the robot
while the corresponding instruction is active.
It is classified as one of six categories:

0: Catastrophic
1: Very bad
2: Bad
3: Ok
4: Good
5: Perfect

This is a fundamentally subjective and not clearly defined task. So it'll
be inevitable that I'll have a slightly different opinion. I try to only
reject labels that are very different from my opinion.

Here is some specific feedback to the questions:
"As stated in the guideline, we
are supposed to give a score of
1 if the item is dropped before
the instruction time ends, but we
were instructed to give a score
of 2 instead.": This depends on the exact situation. For example, it would
be very annoying to most people if the robot is told to pick up a glass but
it drops it and it breaks. I would personally label that as a 1. A 0 or 2
might also be understandable. However, this is certainly not a 3, 4, or 5.
I don't know anyone who would be "OK" with this kind of behavior.

"According to the guidelines, if a
robot takes more than two
attempts to complete the task,
we should give a score of 2, but
they are now instructing us to
give a score of 3.": This depends also on the situation. If the task is to
pick up something, and the robot has to readjust the grasp slightly, it
could be a 3 or even a 4. It shouldn't be a 5 since the behavior is clearly
not "Perfect". A 2 would be understandable maybe. A 1 would not make sense
in this context. Humans have to make adjustments all the time. This is
certainly not "very bad".
